course_title: Human Function in Health & Disease B
course_description: PHYL2067 will provide an overview of human diseases in relation to physiological systems. Students will examine: 1) movement and its associated problems, 2) the role of hormones in physical disease and stress, 3) burns and pain, and 4) the renal system in health and aging.

learning_outcomes.description: Knowledge - Explain how physiological dysfunctions can result in stress and disease including obesity, diabetes, and disorders of movement.
Knowledge - Demonstrate an understanding of how physiological dysfunctions can result in stress and diseases including obesity, diabetes and disorders of movement.
Knowledge - Evaluate how disease states can impact on daily living, and how occupational therapists can communicate their role.
Knowledge - Test the assertions made in lectures and textbooks and to establish the conditions under which these assertions might or might not apply.
Practicality - Integrate laboratory data with the theory of physiology.
Metacognition - Reflect effectively on your learning in physiology.

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
You must submit your Assessment task, with the electronic coversheet available on the School's website (under Undergraduate - Assessment), to Turnitin by the submission deadline. You may submit drafts to Turnitin up to the due date, but you will only be able to submit once on or after the due date. You should also keep an electronic copy of every piece of assessment you submit.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
A request for an extension must be submitted through my.UQ as soon as it becomes evident that an extension is needed, but no later than 24 hours after the assessment task submission due date and time.
Requests for extension received more than 24 hours after the assessment task submission due date and time will not be accepted for consideration unless you provide evidence of exceptional circumstances preventing you from submitting a request prior to the deadline, e.g., due to hospitalisation.
If you have been granted an extension, then the assessment specified penalty listed under Late Submission will be applied to submissions made after the due date/time of the approved extension.
If you are wanting to make a new submission during your extension period after a previous submission prior to the approved extension, please send your assessment to sbms@enquire.uq.edu.au so we can assist with uploading it for you. Please note submission date/time will be when you sent us the email with your submission.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
If you are experiencing technical difficulties uploading your submission, please email a copy of your assessment to sbms@enquire.uq.edu.au so this can be logged on your behalf. Please be advised that date/time of submission will be the date/time you send the email with your submission.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 2 (27 Jul - 09 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Module 1: Movement and Posture Mary-Louise Roy Manchadi and Shyuan Ngo 4hrs of independent study lectures (Brain control of movement and posture, Parkinson's and Huntington's diseases, other movement disorders), plus a live on campus activity (15min) for course introduction in week 1 (Shyuan Ngo), and live on campus activity movement lectorial in week 2.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 3 To Week 6 (10 Aug - 06 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Module 2: Endocrinology Shyuan Ngo and Louise Ainscough Shyuan Ngo - 4hrs of lectures on campus (Introduction to the Endocrine System; Thyroid Function and Metabolism; Stress) Louise Ainscough - 4hrs of independent study lectures (Diabetes and Obesity; Growth, Bones and Ageing).

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 3 To Week 4 (10 Aug - 23 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Reflexes and balance In this practical, you will test your iris reflexes, stretch reflexes, ulnar nerve conduction velocity, balance and motor control. Practical group 1 will attend in week 3, and group 2 will attend in week 4. PPE required: Closed in shoes. You do not need your lab coat or safety glasses.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 5 To Week 6 (24 Aug - 06 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Oral glucose tolerance test In this practical, you will be measuring your blood glucose levels after taking a glucose load. This practical works best if you fast in the morning before the test. Practical group 1 will attend in week 5, and group 2 will attend in week 6. PPE required: You will need your laboratory coat, safety glasses and closed in shoes.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 8 To Week 11 (14 Sep - 18 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Module 3: Wound healing, Burns, Pain and Inflammation Louise Ainscough 4hrs of independent study lectures (Skin; Wound healing and Burns; Pain), plus a lectorial on campus in week 11.
Assignment Information Session Louise Ainscough In this on campus lecture we will go through the requirements of the information sheet assignment. This is your chance to ask questions!

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 10 To Week 13 (05 Oct - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Module 4: Renal system and Ageing Louise Ainscough 6hrs of independent study lectures (Renal physiology; Dehydration; Chronic kidney disease; Urinary incontinence), plus a lectorial on campus in week 13.
